logp.method_description: The log Po/w values were estimated by the shake-flask method, according to reported procedures [77]. Weighed amounts (ca. 1 mg) of all the Ru(III) compounds were dissolved at a concentration of 0.5 mg/mL in the solvent optimal for its solubilization: thus, the lipophilic Ru(III) complexes were dissolved in n-octanol, while AziRu in a saline buffered solution (i.e., 10 mM KH2PO4/K2HPO4, 100 mM NaCl, pH = 7.3). Then, an equal volume of saline solution was added to the Ru(III) complexes dissolved in the organic phase, and of n-octanol to the AziRu aqueous solution: these solutions were then mechanically shaken at r.t. for 2 h. The typical shake-flask protocol requires 24 h mixing of the different phases. However, to minimize the effects of ligand-exchange processes, a mixing time of 2 h was used in these experiments [78]. Subsequently, the mixtures were left to equilibrate for 30 min. Considering the t1/2 value of AziRu, calculated as <1 h, only for this compound, a mixing time of 30 min followed by equilibration for 15 min was used. After separation, the phase in which each compound was originally dissolved was analyzed by UV–vis spectroscopy. The absorption values before and after partitioning were compared and, based on the Lambert–Beer Law, allowed the calculation of the log Po/w values. Each experiment was repeated at least in triplicate.
